R07: Shutdown request publication and its monotonic start must not wait for dispatch-owned locks, log, or perform dependency I/O.

For re-entrant Python signal delivery, first-write-wins means the signal that wins the handler's first atomic publication claim. Claim state is preallocated, and an earlier handler invocation interrupted before reaching the claim is not considered published.
A dispatch transaction is linearized when it enters its guard. A transaction entered before shutdown is bounded in-flight work; transactions entering afterward are rejected.

Startup Kafka, Schema Registry, and reconciliation dependency operations use the same dispatch rule: authorize and submit only bounded executor work inside the guard, run native work outside it, and abandon the remaining startup sequence when shutdown rejects submission.
Startup dependency execution has a dedicated executor factory seam and must not consume or replace the runtime Kafka executor factory used by worker-generation lifecycle tests and ownership.

Kafka-backed logging is prepared through the guarded startup lane but remains detached until all startup dependency and worker-construction stages complete, preventing startup log records from bypassing dispatch authorization.
Native dependency operations never execute inside the dispatch guard.
All shutdown waits derive from one absolute deadline that later cleanup stages cannot extend.
Cooperative workers close their own consumers. Permanently wedged native calls are abandoned behind daemon execution boundaries and are not cross-thread closed.

Runtime cleanup is deliberately two-phase: reject and cancel queued executor work without waiting, close the worker pool so borrowed consumers are marked for owner-thread closure, then wait for cooperative workers behind the daemon lifecycle boundary. Existing regression expectations must verify this ordered sequence.
R28, not R07, owns shutdown effects on /live and /ready.
R28: Liveness resolves the authoritative shutdown callback in both imported src.main mode and the documented python -m src.main execution mode, where the runtime module is registered as __main__.
R36: Readiness observes the same authoritative shutdown-request publication as liveness and returns HTTP 503 immediately when shutdown wins, without waiting for lifecycle finalization to update HealthStateStore.
R41: Scheduler capacity is detached store-owned state, not a live snapshot callback. Topology transitions atomically publish expected partitions and their corresponding scheduler-capacity value under the HealthStateStore lock.
R88: A recreated-topic replacement runtime is a distinct Kafka dependency transaction: authorize and submit it through the shared shutdown dispatch guard, run native construction outside the guard on an abandonable daemon lane, and skip reconstruction when shutdown wins first.
